source.code: uint64_t unpacksize = compute_chunk_unpack_size (y, cinfo->width, cinfo->height, lpc, part);
source.description: Project code consumes attacker-controlled scanline chunk metadata and channel sampling state from the accepted file to derive the chunk's uncompressed byte count.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled OpenEXR chunk metadata and channel descriptors parsed from the input file into `cinfo` and `part`.

root_cause.description: The decode path allocates the heap unpack buffer exactly to `decode->chunk.unpacked_size` and performs no source-backed check here that later `generic_unpack` row consumption stays within that span.

sink.description: `generic_unpack` reads channel samples from `srcbuffer` after the pointer has advanced past the heap allocation sized from `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`.

fine_trace.code: uint64_t unpacksize = compute_chunk_unpack_size (y, cinfo->width, cinfo->height, lpc, part);
fine_trace.note: For an admitted scanline chunk, project code uses parsed chunk geometry and channel sampling state from the file to materialize the byte count that will later govern unpack-buffer sizing.
The computed `unpacksize` is stored into the chunk descriptor as the authoritative uncompressed-size field for this decode path, with no later adjustment in this function.
The decode path allocates `decode->unpacked_buffer` exactly to `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`; the saved ASan trace records the witness heap allocation as 21 bytes.

After the chunk has been read and the unpack buffer prepared, decode dispatches into the unpack routine without a separate bounds validation comparing future `srcbuffer` consumption against `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`.

Inside `generic_unpack`, each admitted sampled row for each channel consumes `w * bpc` bytes from `srcbuffer`; skipped rows `continue`, while rows that pass the `cury % decc->y_samples == 0` test reach the later read and then advance the pointer by `w * bpc`.

`UNPACK_SAMPLES (w)` dereferences `srcbuffer` for the admitted row. In the reproduced crash, ASan reports a 4-byte read 2 bytes past the 21-byte heap allocation made for `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`, proving this read exceeded the allocated unpack span.

format.contract: An accepted scanline OpenEXR input that reaches `generic_unpack` and causes `UNPACK_SAMPLES (w)` to read 4 bytes from `srcbuffer` after it has advanced past the heap allocation created for `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`.
format.name: OpenEXR file

poc.trigger: Run the saved PoC through `openexr_exrcorecheck_fuzzer`; the accepted scanline decode path reaches `generic_unpack` and triggers the ASan out-of-bounds read.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in generic_unpack (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/unpack.c): while unpacking/decoding image data (via exr_decoding_run / readCoreScanlinePart), generic_unpack performs an out-of-bounds read of 4 bytes past a heap-allocated buffer. This insufficient bounds checking / incorrect buffer sizing can cause crashes, memory corruption and may enable information disclosure or further exploitation when parsing crafted OpenEXR files.
bug_description.normalized: A crafted scanline OpenEXR file reaches `generic_unpack`, which reads past the heap unpack buffer allocated from `decode->chunk.unpacked_size`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.summary: ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at `generic_unpack` in `unpack.c:1168`. The accessed address is 2 bytes past a 21-byte heap allocation made by `internal_decode_alloc_buffer` during `exr_decoding_run`.
